title: Docs + import: bring a Tormach PathPilot tool table (.csv export) into CamCraft, and back

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Asked by mkinney (2026-11-18): "Can you create a p3 doc issue for that tools export. If you can import tools, add that too. I might want to import tools for future tests on hub."

## What a Tormach user has today

PathPilot can export and import its whole tool table as a `.csv` file (Tormach 770MX operator manual UM10587, section 7.6.4 "Import and Export the Tool Table"): **Offsets tab -> Export -> type a name -> save to a USB drive**; **Import** on the same tab loads a `.csv` back. PathPilot Hub has the same Offsets tab.

CamCraft today:
- imports and exports tool libraries only as `.camtools` (`import_tool_library`, `export_tool_library`, #355, #899);
- writes a setup's tool list as a generic CSV for a spreadsheet (`tool_list_export.rs`, #389) - not PathPilot's column layout;
- has no docs page that tells a Tormach user how to get his machine's tools into CamCraft.

So a user re-types every tool (number, diameter, length, description) to make posted programs match the machine.

## What to do

1. **Docs** (site guide, Tormach section): how to export the PathPilot tool table (the steps above), how to bring it into CamCraft, and how the tool numbers map to `T<n>` in the posted program. Same page: the reverse, for PathPilot Hub tests.
2. **Import:** read a PathPilot tool-table `.csv` into the document's tools (or a `.camtools` library): tool number, diameter, length/offset, type and description where the file has them; the user completes what PathPilot does not store (flutes, flute length, holder). One undo step; an MCP tool (or a format option on `import_tool_library`); refuse by name a row it cannot read.
3. **Export (for Hub and the real machine):** write the document's tools as a PathPilot tool-table `.csv` that PathPilot's Import reads, so a Hub test or a real job starts with the same tool numbers and diameters as the posted program.

## Open point

The exact PathPilot CSV columns are not in the manual. mkinney will export his 770MX tool table; that file is the sample to build and pin the parser against (tests with a recorded `.csv`, no machine needed).

Done means: a docs page with the export/import steps; an import that reads the sample file into tools with the right numbers and diameters, pinned by a test; an export that PathPilot Hub imports (checked once in Hub).

The review uses "may". It does not confirm wrong output. This issue has no `bug` label for that reason.

- Either the windows line up across the boundary, or the short tab gets a `tabs:` note.

title: Contour tabs: the bridge check compares only neighbouring cuts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

The bridge check in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_bridge.rs` came with PR #2486. It compares only two neighbouring cuts: the cut before a tab and the cut after it.

The check reads only the last `W + D` of the walk before the tab. It reads only the first `W + D` of the walk after the tab. Lead-in and lead-out moves are included.

A different cut can come closer than the tab width. The check does not read that cut. Two cases are known:

- A U-turn of the same ring. A later part of the ring comes near the tab.
- A different ring at the same level.

The reviewer of head `613ba4abf` says that the tab then holds through a strip that is narrower than W. Main had the same limit before PR #2486. The decision file `docs/decisions/2480-tab-bridge-width.md` records this limit.

## Cases seen in the build review (not confirmed as tab necks)

- A 60 x 7 mm inside slot, W = 3 mm, 3 mm tabs. Two cut runs are 2.06 mm apart. The output has no note. The reviewer says the ring is almost a line here, so the distance is across the slot. The reviewer did not confirm a tab neck.
- An inside L-shape with Perpendicular, Arc or Tangential leads. Lead cuts on the two walls of a 14 mm arm come within 0.07 to 3.4 mm of each other. The cuts are in scrap material, far from the tabs. The reviewer says this was present before PR #2486 and is not a bridge failure.

## First step

Write a shape-mask test in `crates/motion/tests/common/shape_mask.rs` (see AGENTS.md, "2D toolpath shape-mask tests"). Use the U-turn case and the second-ring case. Measure the narrowest bridge.

- If no bridge is narrower than the tab width, post the result on this issue. Keep P3.
- If a bridge is narrower than the tab width, raise this issue to P1. AGENTS.md sets P1 for unsafe output.

## Smaller points

- [ ] `SLACK = 1e-6` (`tab_bridge.rs:77`) has no margin for arc chord error. The reviewer found no bridge under W in a probe, but says the margin is small.
- [ ] With a picked start, the windows grow backward only (`tab_bridge.rs:104`, `128-129`). If the first window grows past the pick, the first keep no longer starts at the pick. No note says this. `contour.rs:307-309` then checks `lead_held` on a keep that is not at the pick. The reviewer says this is not a gouge. Add a `tabs:` note, or a refusal by name.
- [ ] No test has more than one tabbed level. The tests in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_bridge.rs` use TAB_H = 1 and a stepdown of 2. The reviewer's probe with three levels gave a correct result. Add a test with more than one tabbed level.

## Done means

- The shape-mask result is posted on this issue.
- Each smaller point is fixed, or has a `tabs:` note or a named refusal, with a test that pins it.

Refs #2480
Found in the reviews of PR #2486.

body:
The maintainer asked for this research on 2026-11-18. It is the second GPU research issue, after #2525 (nesting).

Question: can a GPU shader generate or help to generate the toolpaths of operations?

Open questions for the research:
- Candidates: find which operation steps map to the GPU. Examples: a height field of the model (drop-cutter, tool-offset field), 2D offset by distance field (pocket, contour, adaptive clearing), rest-material and stock removal fields, collision and gouge checks over a grid.
- Accuracy: a grid has a resolution limit. What resolution holds the tolerance of an operation (for example 0.01 mm over a 500 mm part)? Can an exact check with the vector or mesh geometry remove each risk? A toolpath that gouges is the worst failure (Prime Directive).
- Speed: compare with the CPU generators of `camcraft-motion` and `camcraft-cl`. Estimate the gain for each candidate on the large fixtures. Include the cost of the transfer between CPU and GPU.
- Platform: the project builds on Windows, Linux and macOS, and in the browser build (wgpu). Which compute path works on all of them? Issues #2424 and #74 show that GPU drivers fail on some machines. What happens with no GPU or a bad adapter (CPU fallback, refusal with a diagnostic)?
- Determinism: the same input must give the same toolpath and the same G-code on each machine. Do GPU results differ between drivers (float rules)? How do we pin this with golden files in `tests/golden/`?
- Architecture: where does the code live (a new crate, or `camcraft-motion`)? Which dependency would it add? A new `camcraft-*` dependency needs a decision entry. How does the work fit the command model and the stock simulation?
- Relation to the existing simulation: the stock simulation may already use the GPU. Find what exists, and what can be shared.

Done means: comments on this issue answer each question above, with sources. The research ends with a recommendation (use, do not use, or use only as a preview or first filter before an exact CPU result) and the follow-up issues, each with one `P*` and one `effort:*` label. Then close this issue.

Use only published literature and general knowledge (Clean-Room Protocol).

- Accuracy: a bitmap has a resolution limit. Can the method keep a safe gap (kerf, tool radius, lead-in) with no overlap? What resolution does a 3 m sheet need for 0.1 mm? Can a final exact check with the vector geometry (`camcraft-geometry`) remove each risk?
- Speed: compare with the NFP method of #2158. Estimate the gain for 50, 200 and 1000 parts and for the rotation set.
- Platform: the project must build on Windows, Linux and macOS, and in the browser build (wgpu). Which GPU API and which compute or render path works on all of them? What happens when no GPU exists (CPU fallback)?
- Determinism: the same input must give the same layout on each machine (`#2164`). Do GPU results differ between drivers? How do we pin this?
- Layer rule: where does the code live (`camcraft-geometry` or a new crate)? Which dependency would it add? A new dependency needs a decision entry.
- Features: grain (#2398), vacuum zones (#2404), holes that hold parts, remnant sheets (#2164).

Done means: comments on this issue answer each question above, with sources. The research ends with a recommendation (use, do not use, or use only as a first filter before the exact check) and the follow-up issues, each with one `P*` and one `effort:*` label. Then close this issue.

Use only published literature and general knowledge (Clean-Room Protocol).

title: 2D Contour tabs: the bridge on the part is tab width minus the tool diameter; a tab width <= D leaves no tab and frees the part

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## Problem

2D Contour tabs are narrower than the "Tab width" that the user sets. At its narrowest section (the centre line of the cut channel) the tab is `tab_width - tool diameter` wide. When the tab width is equal to or less than the tool diameter, no tab stays. The part comes free during the last levels, and no message tells the user.

## Cause

`Ring::tab_keeps` and `Ring::tab_keeps_from_start` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring.rs`) measure the tab window on the tool-centre ring. At each end of that window the cutter disc removes `D/2` more material along the centre line of the channel. The bridge is thus `tab_width` wide at the part wall, but only `tab_width - D` wide at the channel centre line.

Example: a 6 mm end mill and a tab width of 5 mm. The window on the centre path is 5 mm long. On the channel centre line the cutter removes 3 mm on each side past the window ends. The two cuts overlap by 1 mm (5 - 6 = -1 mm), so the bridge is cut through.

## Expected result

The tab width is the smallest width of the bridge that stays. For this, the window on the centre ring must be `tab_width + D` long.

If a tab cannot stay (for example, the window with the tool diameter is longer than the tab spacing), refuse the operation by name. Do not cut the part free silently.

## Related

- #1565: Verify and the stock sim do not find a piece of stock that the program frees. Thus this defect is not found by verify either.

## Proposed priority

`P1` by the AGENTS.md table: wrong output that passes. A freed part can move into the cutter.

I can make the fix and a test (shape-mask test of the bridge width) in a PR from my fork.

body:
What happens: a model does not remember the file that it came from. `ImportModel` keeps the name, the mesh and the import settings only (`crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`). When the source file changes, the user must import it again by hand.

Expected:
- An imported model keeps its source path and the SHA-256 of the file that it read. The `.camproj` file saves the two values. A project that has no values still opens.
- While the project is open, CamCraft checks the source file of each model. When the file has a new hash, CamCraft imports it again through `CommandKind::ImportFile`, under the same model name. The existing update path marks the operations Stale.

- A source file that is missing or that CamCraft cannot read does not change the model. The status line says so by name, one time.
- The user can turn off the update for a model ("Unlink").
- An MCP tool reads and sets the link.

Why: Solidcraft proposes "Send to CamCraft" (Solidcraft RFC 0001, phases 1 and 3: https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0001-craft-bridge.md). Each save in Solidcraft writes the `.sc` file again. With this issue, CamCraft updates the part after each save.

Depends on: the issue for opening a model file from the command line (#2462).

Done means: a test changes a source file and finds the model updated and its operations Stale; a test finds an unchanged model when the file is missing; a `.camproj` round trip keeps the link; an older `.camproj` opens.

A tool with no number of its own posts as its 1-based position in the document's tool list (`crates/app/src/tool_numbers.rs`, #221), and that list is in name order. A tool's posted number is stable once the tool is in the document: e.g. `add_tool` gives the next free number (and says so), or unnumbered tools keep the number they first posted with, and a post with unnumbered tools says which numbers it assumed.

## What happens

A through hole drilled with a twist drill only gets the fixed break-through below the part bottom (1.0 mm by default, #1557). The drill's point length is not added, so full diameter never reaches the bottom: with a 6 mm 118 deg drill the point is 3 / tan(59 deg) = 1.80 mm long, the tip stops at z -1 and full diameter ends at z +0.8. Each "through" hole leaves a ~0.8 mm cone/lip at the exit. Generate and verify say ok.

Also: the `break_through` parameter from #1557 is not listed by `list_operation_types` for Drill (its default is `null`, so the field is skipped), so an MCP agent cannot find it; the QA agent reported "no break-through option".

## Expected

For a through hole, the depth puts the full diameter at least the break-through below the bottom: bottom - break_through - point length (from the tool's tip angle and diameter), or a stated choice between "tip" and "full diameter"; and `list_operation_types` lists `break_through`.

**Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). ### What are you trying to do

I picked the shipped grblHAL machine for a setup that posted with Fanuc. The setup kept Fanuc, and nothing suggested the grblHAL post. A `.mch` file cannot say which post goes with it. `post_offer` offers `default_post_for(kind)` only when the current post does not serve the machine's kind, so for every mill the offer is Fanuc. The pairings exist only as comments in `MACHINES`. #1915 and #1918 expect `default_post_for` to map machines to their post, but it takes only the kind.

### How you imagine it working

- An optional key, for example `controller.post: "grblHAL"`, names a post in `BUILTINS`. Without the key, nothing changes.
- `validate_text` refuses, naming the key, a name not in the registry and a post that does not serve the machine's kind.

What happens: The grblHAL and Tormach posts write a G86 block with no P word when the bore dwell is 0 (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps` and `assets/posts/tormach.cps`, `onCycle`). Each new G86 block comes after G80.

The LinuxCNC interpreter requires P on the first G86 block of a cycle. `src/emc/rs274ngc/interp_cycles.cc`, `convert_cycle_xy`:

```
CHKS(((settings->motion_mode != G_86) && (block->p_number == -1.0)),
    NCE_DWELL_TIME_P_WORD_MISSING_WITH_G86);
```

The LinuxCNC G-code reference gives the format `G86 ... R- L- P- $-` and lists "a P number is required" as a canned-cycle error. grblHAL follows the LinuxCNC specification for its canned cycles.

Expected: A bore with a dwell of 0 posts a program that the control accepts. One option is `P0` on G86 (the LinuxCNC reference permits a P that is not negative). Check the grblHAL code list for G86 first.

Priority: `P3`. The control stops the program with an error. The output is not a silent wrong motion. The behaviour on a real grblHAL or PathPilot control is not verified.

Evidence: Found during the work on #2360. The G86 goldens of `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (grblhal, tormach) show G86 with no P.

Done means: A test pins the G86 P word for a zero dwell on the two posts, and the goldens agree.

- A Rotate mode in the bottom bar of the viewport, next to the Move button of PR #1330.

**How it must fit the laws**
- Everything Is a Command: the drag is an ephemeral preview while the button is down. The release queues ONE undoable command: the same `MoveModel` that the Model page's rotation fields run. No direct field write.
- Escape during a drag cancels with no history step. A drag that ends at its start angle adds no history step.
- The rotation changes the placement in the same way as a typed rotation: operations become stale, and stock and fixtures follow as they do now. No new placement path.
- A handle under the cursor wins the press. Empty space still orbits. The handles keep a constant size on screen.
- While the user drags, the bar shows the angle.
- If a new app command is necessary, it gets its MCP tool (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool"). The MCP `move_model` tool already sets the rotation.
- Pin the behaviour in structural and interaction tests, not in PNG snapshots.

Depends on PR #1330 (the Move mode and the `move_drag` module). Stack on that PR, or start after it merges.

Done means: a drag on a rotation handle of the selected part turns the part about the axis, one undo step for each drag, and interaction tests pin the handles, the angle and the undo step.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
